title: Normalized direct-image square is the pullback mate
statement: For schemes X,Y,X′,Y′ [def-pc-scheme] and morphisms f:X→Y, f′:X′→Y′, g:Y′→Y, gX:X′→X with gX;f=f′;g, let a be the pinned derived pullback/direct-image adjunction [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] and p the fixed pullback composition comparison [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. The conjugate of p(f′,g);transport;p(gX,f)⁻¹ under a(f)∘a(gX) and a(g)∘a(f′) equals e(gX,f);transport;e(f′,g)⁻¹, where e is the comparison selected with its right-derived-unit equation [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition]. There is no global-sections functor in this assertion.

proof.text: For each composable pair, apply the single-pair mate unit equation. It uses the same pinned pullback composition and adjunctions as the statement.

The chosen direct-image comparison has exactly this inverse-unit equation by exists_derivedModuleDirectImageComposition. Functor.rightDerived_ext applied to the derived direct image of the composite identifies the mate of the pullback comparison hom with the direct-image comparison inverse. This uses uniqueness out of the single right-derived functor, so no additional cancellation on K-injective representatives is necessary here.

Use Iso.ext on conjugateIsoEquiv and take inverse morphisms to obtain the mate equation for the inverse pullback comparison. For equality transport, substitute equal scheme morphisms and use conjugateEquiv_id. These steps are written in Lean as the local facts hi and he.

Reassociate the three-factor pullback square, then apply conjugateEquiv_comp twice, through the adjunctions of gX ≫ f and f′ ≫ g. Substitute the inverse comparison, the equality transport, and the forward comparison equations. This is exactly the three-factor normalized direct-image square, with the original statement unchanged.

proof_origin.note: Decomposition of the existing normalization argument: the single-pair unit calculation is split off, and the right-derived uniqueness, inverse conjugacy, equality transport and three-factor assembly are proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem derivedDirectImage_square_mate
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (gX : X' ⟶ X)
    (h : gX ≫ f = f' ≫ g) :
    let a := fun {A D : Scheme.{u}} (t : A ⟶ D) ↦ schemeHomPullbackAdjunction t
    let p := @Classical.choose _ _ (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec
      (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition.{u, w})))
    let k := p f' g ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun t ↦ derivedPullback t) h.symm) ≪≫ (p gX f).symm
    let e₁ : schemeDerivedDirectImage gX ⋙ schemeDerivedDirectImage f ≅
        schemeDerivedDirectImage (gX ≫ f) :=
      schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso gX f
    let e₂ : schemeDerivedDirectImage f' ⋙ schemeDerivedDirectImage g ≅
        schemeDerivedDirectImage (f' ≫ g) :=
      schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso f' g
    conjugateEquiv ((a f).comp (a gX)) ((a g).comp (a f')) k.hom =
      e₁.hom ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (fun t ↦ schemeDerivedDirectImage t) h) ≫ e₂.inv
